content_html:
Five checks your AI-agent setup needs before it runs — one command.

Five things quietly go wrong in an AI-agent setup before anyone notices: a folder that executes code the moment it is opened, a live API key sitting in a config file, a safety hook that was never going to fire, two agents a router cannot tell apart, a skill collection too sprawled to discover anything in. Each used to need its own tool — five of mine, all published separately, all sitting quiet. Now one command runs all five audits and prints a single combined receipt:

preflight-agent scan ~/my-project

Static and read-only — a scan executes nothing. No module runs, imports, or installs anything in the target; the reports cite what they found instead of judging intent. And the verdicts are honest about their edges: a module with nothing to audit reports skipped with its reason, never clean, and every module prints its own limits in its own section of the receipt.

Watch it run

One scan of the fixture with exactly one planted problem per module — an auto-run .envrc, a literal key in .mcp.json, a guard hook pointing at a script that does not exist, a duplicated agent name, a duplicated skill name — five modules, five findings, one combined receipt (29 seconds, real run, nothing staged).

The receipt family

preflight-agent is the before it runs member of a family built on one grammar — document = claims, code = evidence, every verdict cited:

  • preflight-agent — is this setup safe to open? The five preflight checks below, in one receipt.
  • skill-vet — is this skill pack dangerous? Stealing, spying, hidden sending, each proven as a combination of evidence before you install.
  • permission-audit — do these permissions grant more than intended? Audits a Claude Code allowlist chain: wildcard grants, dangerous modes, rules that can never fire.
  • done-claim-auditor — did the agent do what it claimed? Claim-vs-evidence logic pointed at session transcripts.
  • skill-claims — does a skill do what it claims? Audits a skill's prose promises against its static behaviour.
  • spec-receipt — does the code still match the spec? Audits a repo's engineering spec against its declared implementation surfaces.

Quick start

pipx install preflight-agent           # or: pip install preflight-agent
preflight-agent scan path/to/setup

(Live on PyPI since v1.0.1. Source checkouts also work — pipx install git+https://github.com/jasveerai88/preflight-agent — or run from source: python3 src/preflight_agent.py scan <dir>.)

One command, one receipt, an exit code you can gate on — 1 = at least one module has findings, 0 = every module that ran is clean, 2 = usage/input error. Add --json for a machine-readable receipt. Python 3.10+, standard library only, no dependencies, no network.

The five modules

Every module is also runnable on its own, with exactly the interface its standalone tool had:

Command What it catches Its verdict words
preflight-agent clone-guard DIR What executes when this folder is opened, installed, or committed to: Claude / VS Code / devcontainer configs, npm install scripts, direnv, git and husky hooks — every command shown verbatim AUTO-RUN / INSTALL-TIME / PRESENT / UNPARSEABLE
preflight-agent secret-guard scan FILE... Inline secrets in agent/MCP config files — findings by key path and fingerprint; values are never printed INLINE-SECRET / ENV-LITERAL / UNPARSEABLE
preflight-agent secret-guard fix FILE... [--apply] Rewrites those literals as ${ENV_VAR} references. Dry run unless --apply; a timestamped backup is kept beside each changed file, and the rewrite is re-scanned before it is reported — (the suite's one writing command; see the exception below)
preflight-agent hook-doctor audit SETTINGS [--home DIR] Claude Code hooks that can never fire, can never block, or point at files that do not exist ERROR / WARNING / INFO
preflight-agent fleet-audit audit FOLDER In a folder of agent definitions: description collisions, duplicate names, tool grants that contradict the promised job, unreadable files ERROR / WARNING / INFO
preflight-agent skill-sprawl audit FOLDER In a tree of skills: cross-scope duplicate names, discovery collisions, oversized bodies, and a discovery-budget truncation forecast ERROR / WARNING / INFO

The combined scan

preflight-agent scan DIR [--home DIR] [--json]

scan points each module at the part of DIR it audits:

  • clone-guard — DIR itself.
  • secret-guard — every discovered config file: settings.json, settings.local.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json anywhere under DIR, plus any JSON inside a .claude, .vscode or .cursor folder. Scan only — the combined scan never calls fix.
  • hook-doctor — the first of .claude/settings.json, settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json. --home defaults to DIR itself, so a self-contained setup is audited as its own home.
  • fleet-audit — .claude/agents, else agents, else DIR itself.
  • skill-sprawl — .claude/skills, else skills, else DIR itself.

The fixture — one planted problem per module

examples/make_fixture.py builds a fake setup with exactly one planted problem per module — an .envrc that runs on cd, a literal service key in .mcp.json, a PreToolUse guard pointing at a script that does not exist, the agent name reviewer defined twice, the skill name notes-writer defined in two scopes — and everything else deliberately clean. Verbatim output of the real run (build it yourself and diff):

$ python3 examples/make_fixture.py pf-fixture
fixture built at pf-fixture
$ preflight-agent scan pf-fixture
preflight-agent v1.0.1 — scan · folder pf-fixture
5 module(s) run · 0 clean · 5 with findings · 0 skipped

===== clone-guard — what runs when this folder is opened =====
clone-guard v0.1.0 — scan · folder pf-fixture
pf-fixture · 3 finding(s) — 3 AUTO-RUN · 0 INSTALL-TIME · 0 PRESENT · 0 UNPARSEABLE

AUTO-RUN — executes on open, session start or cd, with no install step (3):
  .claude/settings.json — Claude Code PreToolUse hook — runs automatically when Claude Code works in this folder
    command: python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  .claude/settings.json — Claude Code SessionStart hook — runs automatically when Claude Code works in this folder
    command: echo session started
  .envrc — direnv file — direnv executes it automatically when you cd into this folder (when direnv is installed and the folder is allowed)
    1 line(s) of shell — direnv sources the whole file; open it to inspect

VERDICT: FINDINGS — read every command above before opening this folder in an editor or with an agent.
clone-guard only reads files: it never executes, installs or modifies anything in the scanned folder. Findings are auto-execution surfaces, not proof of malice — legitimate projects use hooks and install scripts too. The command text is the evidence; judge it.

===== secret-guard — inline secrets in agent/MCP configs =====
secret-guard v0.1.0 — scan · 2 file(s)
1 finding(s) — 0 INLINE-SECRET · 1 ENV-LITERAL · 0 UNPARSEABLE

ENV-LITERAL — a secret-shaped literal in an env block, whatever the key is named (1):
  pf-fixture/.mcp.json — mcpServers.notes.env.SERVICE_KEY
    key "SERVICE_KEY" holds a literal secret: Q7…(24 chars). Fix rewrites it as the SERVICE_KEY environment variable.

VERDICT: FINDINGS — move each value into the named environment variable (run the fix command to rewrite the files), and rotate any secret that was ever committed or shared: moving it does not un-leak it.
secret-guard never prints a secret's value: reports show the key path and a fingerprint (first characters + length) only.

===== hook-doctor — dead hooks and guards that cannot block =====
hook-doctor v0.1.0 — audit · settings settings.json
2 hook handlers across 2 events · home for ~ and $HOME paths: pf-fixture
Read-only: it edits nothing and never runs a hook command. It reads the settings file, plus the scripts that file itself names.

ERRORS — hooks that can never work as configured (1):
[COMMAND_PATH] PreToolUse · matcher "Bash" · python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  the command path $HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh does not exist (resolved against the settings folder and the home folder) — this hook can never run
  fix: create the script at that path, or point the command at a script that exists

WARNINGS — hooks that probably do not do what you intend (1):
[EXIT_CODE_TRAP] PreToolUse · matcher "Bash" · python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  guard-intent hook on PreToolUse shows no way to block: no exit 2 and no JSON decision in the command or the script it runs — exit 1 (and every other code) is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds. Heuristic: the intent was read from guard words (guard / block / deny / prevent / forbid / protect) in the command or script
  fix: exit 2 with the reason on stderr, or print a JSON decision (permissionDecision: deny on PreToolUse) when the guard should stop the action

Summary: 2 findings · 1 errors · 1 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 1 error(s): at least one hook is dead as configured. Fix the errors before relying on these hooks.

===== fleet-audit — agent-definition collisions and grants =====
fleet-audit v0.1.0 — audit · folder agents
2 agent files · 2 agents parsed · 0 unrecognized · walk: recursive (subfolders included)
Read-only: it edits nothing and runs nothing. It reads the agent definition files in the folder you point it at — every .md file in the tree is expected to be an agent file in the supported shape.
Similarity: the Jaccard index over each description's set of lowercase alphanumeric word tokens. Collision at 0.50, near-identical at 0.90; the short-description floor is 40 characters. Thresholds and intent words are heuristics — see SKILL.md.

INVENTORY (2):
  reviewer — 112 chars · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: (default) · extra/reviewer.md
  reviewer — 112 chars · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: (default) · reviewer.md

ERRORS — agents that cannot be routed to, collide head-on, or cannot be read (2):
[DESCRIPTION_IDENTICAL] "reviewer" + "reviewer" · extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md
  the descriptions of "reviewer" and "reviewer" are near-identical (token-set similarity 1.000, at or above the 0.90 line) — a router choosing between them has nothing to choose on, so delegation between them is a coin flip
  fix: differentiate the descriptions until each names work the other does not claim — or merge the two agents
[DUPLICATE_NAME] "reviewer" · extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md
  the name "reviewer" is defined by 2 files (extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md) — which definition loads depends on scope order, so the fleet does not reliably contain the agent you think it does
  fix: keep one definition per name in the fleet, or rename until names are unique

Summary: 2 findings · 2 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 2 error(s): the fleet has agents that cannot be routed to, collide head-on, or cannot be read at all. Fix the errors before trusting delegation to this fleet.

===== skill-sprawl — skill duplicates, collisions, bloat =====
skill-sprawl v0.1.0 — audit · folder skills
2 markdown files seen · 2 skill candidates · 2 skills parsed · 0 unrecognized · 0 ignored (supporting docs) · walk: recursive (subfolders included)
Read-only: it edits nothing and runs nothing. It reads the skill definition files in the tree you point it at — files named SKILL.md, plus loose .md files that open with a frontmatter block; other .md files are counted as supporting docs and ignored.
Similarity: the Jaccard index over each description's set of lowercase alphanumeric word tokens. Collision at 0.50, near-identical at 0.90; the short-description floor is 40 characters; the oversized-body line is 500 lines; the discovery budget is 16000 listing characters (a reported figure). Token counts are estimates at chars/4. Thresholds are heuristics — see SKILL.md.

INVENTORY (2):
  notes-writer — 104 desc chars · body 2 lines · ~19 tokens est. · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md
  notes-writer — 104 desc chars · body 2 lines · ~19 tokens est. · notes-writer/SKILL.md
COLLECTION TOTALS: 2 skills · 4 body lines · ~38 tokens of body text (est., chars/4) · discovery listing 232 of 16000 budget chars

ERRORS — skills that cannot be discovered, collide head-on, are defined more than once, or cannot be read (2):
[DESCRIPTION_IDENTICAL] "notes-writer" + "notes-writer" · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md
  the descriptions of "notes-writer" and "notes-writer" are near-identical (token-set similarity 1.000, at or above the 0.90 line) — a router choosing between them has nothing to choose on, so discovery between them is a coin flip
  fix: differentiate the descriptions until each names work the other does not claim — or merge the two skills
[DUPLICATE_NAME] "notes-writer" · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md
  the name "notes-writer" is defined by 2 files (archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md) — which definition loads depends on scope order, so the collection does not reliably contain the skill you think it does
  fix: keep one definition per name across the whole tree, or rename until names are unique

Summary: 2 findings · 2 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 2 error(s): the collection has skills that cannot be discovered, collide head-on, are defined more than once, or cannot be read at all. Fix the errors before trusting discovery in this collection.

VERDICT: FINDINGS in clone-guard, secret-guard, hook-doctor, fleet-audit, skill-sprawl — read each module's section above before this setup runs.
(exit code 1)

The other direction — a clean setup

The same scan over a minimal tidy setup (one agent, one skill, an empty settings file) — head and verdict lines verbatim, module sections elided:

$ preflight-agent scan pf-control
preflight-agent v1.0.1 — scan · folder pf-control
5 module(s) run · 5 clean · 0 with findings · 0 skipped
...
VERDICT: CLEAN — every module that ran reported clean. CLEAN covers only what the five modules check; it is not a guarantee the setup is safe. Each module's limits are in its own section above.
(exit code 0)

Contracts

  • One JSON object per command with --json; argument and input errors are {"error": ...} with exit 2, including argparse errors in --json mode. No tracebacks. A module command's JSON is exactly the object that module printed standalone; scan's JSON nests those objects per module, plus a combined summary and clean verdict.
  • Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 error, identically for every module and for scan.
  • Read-only scanning. No scan writes to, executes, or installs anything in the target.
  • The one disclosed exception: secret-guard fix --apply writes — that is its job. It writes only the files you name, after a dry run by default, keeps a timestamped backup beside each changed file, and re-scans the rewrite before reporting it. It was ported intact from the standalone tool, and scan never invokes it.
  • Deterministic. The same folder produces a byte-identical report on every run.
  • Each module's limits stand. Static checks prove what they cite and no more — every module prints its own honesty limits in its report, and SKILL.md collects them. A CLEAN verdict means "none of the checked problems were found", never "this setup is safe".

Why this suite exists — the merge

This pack is the merged flagship ordered by a fleet audit (FLEET-AUDIT-2026-11-04): 43 published tools were audited, and 18 of the quiet ones were ordered merged into 4 flagships so the fleet would be a few strong tools instead of dozens of shelf orphans. clone-guard, secret-guard, hook-doctor, fleet-audit and skill-sprawl — five standalone auditors, each already shipped and tested — became the modules of this suite.

The merge changed no engine: each module's code is byte-identical to its source tool's, its CLI shape and verdict vocabulary are unchanged, and it still reports its own source version (v0.1.0) inside its sections. The suite's own work is the dispatcher, the combined scan, and 24 new tests on top of the 276 the five source suites carried over — 300 in total.

Known note: the five engines are installed as top-level Python modules (clone_guard, secret_guard, hook_doctor, fleet_audit, skill_sprawl) alongside the preflight_agent dispatcher. If you also installed one of the original standalone tools, both installs provide the same module file with identical content — either copy behaves the same.

For agents

SKILL.md states the full command surface, the verdict vocabularies, the JSON contract and the limits — and makes preflight-agent itself installable as a skill: point your agent at this repo's SKILL.md and it will preflight setups before trusting them.

Install the skill bundle: this repo also ships the same SKILL.md as an installable bundle under skill/. To use it, copy the skill/ folder's SKILL.md into your agent's skills directory (for Claude Code: ~/.claude/skills/preflight-agent/SKILL.md), install the tool with pipx install preflight-agent, and your agent can then run a preflight scan before trusting any setup folder it is handed.

Tests

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

300 tests: the five source suites ported unchanged (56 + 57 + 44 + 58 + 61 = 276 — the only edit is each suite's EXAMPLES path, since examples now live per-module under examples/<module>/) plus 24 dispatcher/scan tests covering target discovery, skipped-with-reason reporting, the combined JSON shape, exit-code aggregation, and the proof that scan never invokes fix. Fixtures are fictional; the secrets in them are fake.

Honest limits

  • Static evidence only. clone-guard reports surfaces that would execute, not what the code does once running; a CLEAN scan is never a safety guarantee.
  • secret-guard's scope is JSON configs it can parse. Values under ordinary key names outside env blocks, and TOML/YAML configs, are out of scope — and a secret that was ever committed stays leaked after moving it: rotate it.
  • hook-doctor judges hooks against a static rule table. It never runs a hook, so runtime behaviour (a script that exists but misbehaves) is invisible to it.
  • fleet-audit / skill-sprawl similarity is a heuristic — a token-set Jaccard index at stated thresholds (collision 0.50, near-identical 0.90, short-description floor 40 chars, discovery budget 16,000 listing chars): a reported figure, not a platform guarantee.
  • scan's discovery is a convention, stated above: it audits the settings/config/agents/skills locations it looks for. A setup that keeps those elsewhere needs the module commands pointed at the real paths.
  • Python-only implementation, terminal-text reports. No daemon, no watcher, no auto-remediation beyond secret-guard fix, no score — a receipt, not a rating.

Contributing

See CONTRIBUTING.md. The evidence discipline is the product: a finding is issued only on what the files show, and contributions are held to that. Found a setup preflight-agent misjudges — a surface it misses, a verdict the evidence doesn't support? Open an issue with the folder (or a minimal fixture); that is exactly the feedback that improves the checks.

Security

preflight-agent is itself an audit tool, so its own posture is simple: it has no network code, no dependencies, and its scans never execute what they read. See SECURITY.md for how to report a problem.

License

MIT — see LICENSE. The five engines keep their original authorship; this merged pack's own history starts at the merge (see CHANGELOG.md).

Related

  • skill-vet — the pre-install danger gate for agent-skill packs.
  • permission-audit — audits a Claude Code permission allowlist for wildcard grants and dangerous modes.
  • done-claim-auditor — audits a coding agent's completion claims against its own transcript.
  • skill-claims — does a skill package do what its description claims?
  • spec-receipt — a drift receipt for spec'd repos: spec vs code, verdict per item.

Support

If preflight-agent catches something in your setup before it runs, consider sponsoring. Sponsorship funds the time to maintain preflight-agent, ship fixes, and build the next checks its users ask for.

content_html_zh:
Five checks your AI-agent setup needs before it runs — one command.

Five things quietly go wrong in an AI-agent setup before anyone notices: a folder that executes code the moment it is opened, a live API key sitting in a config file, a safety hook that was never going to fire, two agents a router cannot tell apart, a skill collection too sprawled to discover anything in. Each used to need its own tool — five of mine, all published separately, all sitting quiet. Now one command runs all five audits and prints a single combined receipt:

preflight-agent scan ~/my-project

Static and read-only — a scan executes nothing. No module runs, imports, or installs anything in the target; the reports cite what they found instead of judging intent. And the verdicts are honest about their edges: a module with nothing to audit reports skipped with its reason, never clean, and every module prints its own limits in its own section of the receipt.

Watch it run

One scan of the fixture with exactly one planted problem per module — an auto-run .envrc, a literal key in .mcp.json, a guard hook pointing at a script that does not exist, a duplicated agent name, a duplicated skill name — five modules, five findings, one combined receipt (29 seconds, real run, nothing staged).

The receipt family

preflight-agent is the before it runs member of a family built on one grammar — document = claims, code = evidence, every verdict cited:

  • preflight-agent — is this setup safe to open? The five preflight checks below, in one receipt.
  • skill-vet — is this skill pack dangerous? Stealing, spying, hidden sending, each proven as a combination of evidence before you install.
  • permission-audit — do these permissions grant more than intended? Audits a Claude Code allowlist chain: wildcard grants, dangerous modes, rules that can never fire.
  • done-claim-auditor — did the agent do what it claimed? Claim-vs-evidence logic pointed at session transcripts.
  • skill-claims — does a skill do what it claims? Audits a skill's prose promises against its static behaviour.
  • spec-receipt — does the code still match the spec? Audits a repo's engineering spec against its declared implementation surfaces.

快速启动

pipx install preflight-agent           # or: pip install preflight-agent
preflight-agent scan path/to/setup

(Live on PyPI since v1.0.1. Source checkouts also work — pipx install git+https://github.com/jasveerai88/preflight-agent — or run from source: python3 src/preflight_agent.py scan <dir>.)

One command, one receipt, an exit code you can gate on — 1 = at least one module has findings, 0 = every module that ran is clean, 2 = usage/input error. Add --json for a machine-readable receipt. Python 3.10+, standard library only, no dependencies, no network.

The five modules

Every module is also runnable on its own, with exactly the interface its standalone tool had:

命令 它捕获什么 Its verdict words
preflight-agent clone-guard DIR What executes when this folder is opened, installed, or committed to: Claude / VS Code / devcontainer configs, npm install scripts, direnv, git and husky hooks — every command shown verbatim AUTO-RUN / INSTALL-TIME / PRESENT / UNPARSEABLE
preflight-agent secret-guard scan FILE... Inline secrets in agent/MCP config files — findings by key path and fingerprint; values are never printed INLINE-SECRET / ENV-LITERAL / UNPARSEABLE
preflight-agent secret-guard fix FILE... [--apply] Rewrites those literals as ${ENV_VAR} references. Dry run unless --apply; a timestamped backup is kept beside each changed file, and the rewrite is re-scanned before it is reported — (the suite's one writing command; see the exception below)
preflight-agent hook-doctor audit SETTINGS [--home DIR] Claude Code hooks that can never fire, can never block, or point at files that do not exist ERROR / WARNING / INFO
preflight-agent fleet-audit audit FOLDER In a folder of agent definitions: description collisions, duplicate names, tool grants that contradict the promised job, unreadable files ERROR / WARNING / INFO
preflight-agent skill-sprawl audit FOLDER In a tree of skills: cross-scope duplicate names, discovery collisions, oversized bodies, and a discovery-budget truncation forecast ERROR / WARNING / INFO

The combined scan

preflight-agent scan DIR [--home DIR] [--json]

scan points each module at the part of DIR it audits:

  • clone-guard — DIR itself.
  • secret-guard — every discovered config file: settings.json, settings.local.json, .mcp.json, mcp.json anywhere under DIR, plus any JSON inside a .claude, .vscode or .cursor folder. Scan only — the combined scan never calls fix.
  • hook-doctor — the first of .claude/settings.json, settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json. --home defaults to DIR itself, so a self-contained setup is audited as its own home.
  • fleet-audit — .claude/agents, else agents, else DIR itself.
  • skill-sprawl — .claude/skills, else skills, else DIR itself.

The fixture — one planted problem per module

examples/make_fixture.py builds a fake setup with exactly one planted problem per module — an .envrc that runs on cd, a literal service key in .mcp.json, a PreToolUse guard pointing at a script that does not exist, the agent name reviewer defined twice, the skill name notes-writer defined in two scopes — and everything else deliberately clean. Verbatim output of the real run (build it yourself and diff):

$ python3 examples/make_fixture.py pf-fixture
fixture built at pf-fixture
$ preflight-agent scan pf-fixture
preflight-agent v1.0.1 — scan · folder pf-fixture
5 module(s) run · 0 clean · 5 with findings · 0 skipped

===== clone-guard — what runs when this folder is opened =====
clone-guard v0.1.0 — scan · folder pf-fixture
pf-fixture · 3 finding(s) — 3 AUTO-RUN · 0 INSTALL-TIME · 0 PRESENT · 0 UNPARSEABLE

AUTO-RUN — executes on open, session start or cd, with no install step (3):
  .claude/settings.json — Claude Code PreToolUse hook — runs automatically when Claude Code works in this folder
    command: python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  .claude/settings.json — Claude Code SessionStart hook — runs automatically when Claude Code works in this folder
    command: echo session started
  .envrc — direnv file — direnv executes it automatically when you cd into this folder (when direnv is installed and the folder is allowed)
    1 line(s) of shell — direnv sources the whole file; open it to inspect

VERDICT: FINDINGS — read every command above before opening this folder in an editor or with an agent.
clone-guard only reads files: it never executes, installs or modifies anything in the scanned folder. Findings are auto-execution surfaces, not proof of malice — legitimate projects use hooks and install scripts too. The command text is the evidence; judge it.

===== secret-guard — inline secrets in agent/MCP configs =====
secret-guard v0.1.0 — scan · 2 file(s)
1 finding(s) — 0 INLINE-SECRET · 1 ENV-LITERAL · 0 UNPARSEABLE

ENV-LITERAL — a secret-shaped literal in an env block, whatever the key is named (1):
  pf-fixture/.mcp.json — mcpServers.notes.env.SERVICE_KEY
    key "SERVICE_KEY" holds a literal secret: Q7…(24 chars). Fix rewrites it as the SERVICE_KEY environment variable.

VERDICT: FINDINGS — move each value into the named environment variable (run the fix command to rewrite the files), and rotate any secret that was ever committed or shared: moving it does not un-leak it.
secret-guard never prints a secret's value: reports show the key path and a fingerprint (first characters + length) only.

===== hook-doctor — dead hooks and guards that cannot block =====
hook-doctor v0.1.0 — audit · settings settings.json
2 hook handlers across 2 events · home for ~ and $HOME paths: pf-fixture
Read-only: it edits nothing and never runs a hook command. It reads the settings file, plus the scripts that file itself names.

ERRORS — hooks that can never work as configured (1):
[COMMAND_PATH] PreToolUse · matcher "Bash" · python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  the command path $HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh does not exist (resolved against the settings folder and the home folder) — this hook can never run
  fix: create the script at that path, or point the command at a script that exists

WARNINGS — hooks that probably do not do what you intend (1):
[EXIT_CODE_TRAP] PreToolUse · matcher "Bash" · python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/guard-rm.sh"
  guard-intent hook on PreToolUse shows no way to block: no exit 2 and no JSON decision in the command or the script it runs — exit 1 (and every other code) is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds. Heuristic: the intent was read from guard words (guard / block / deny / prevent / forbid / protect) in the command or script
  fix: exit 2 with the reason on stderr, or print a JSON decision (permissionDecision: deny on PreToolUse) when the guard should stop the action

Summary: 2 findings · 1 errors · 1 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 1 error(s): at least one hook is dead as configured. Fix the errors before relying on these hooks.

===== fleet-audit — agent-definition collisions and grants =====
fleet-audit v0.1.0 — audit · folder agents
2 agent files · 2 agents parsed · 0 unrecognized · walk: recursive (subfolders included)
Read-only: it edits nothing and runs nothing. It reads the agent definition files in the folder you point it at — every .md file in the tree is expected to be an agent file in the supported shape.
Similarity: the Jaccard index over each description's set of lowercase alphanumeric word tokens. Collision at 0.50, near-identical at 0.90; the short-description floor is 40 characters. Thresholds and intent words are heuristics — see SKILL.md.

INVENTORY (2):
  reviewer — 112 chars · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: (default) · extra/reviewer.md
  reviewer — 112 chars · tools: Read, Grep, Glob · model: (default) · reviewer.md

ERRORS — agents that cannot be routed to, collide head-on, or cannot be read (2):
[DESCRIPTION_IDENTICAL] "reviewer" + "reviewer" · extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md
  the descriptions of "reviewer" and "reviewer" are near-identical (token-set similarity 1.000, at or above the 0.90 line) — a router choosing between them has nothing to choose on, so delegation between them is a coin flip
  fix: differentiate the descriptions until each names work the other does not claim — or merge the two agents
[DUPLICATE_NAME] "reviewer" · extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md
  the name "reviewer" is defined by 2 files (extra/reviewer.md, reviewer.md) — which definition loads depends on scope order, so the fleet does not reliably contain the agent you think it does
  fix: keep one definition per name in the fleet, or rename until names are unique

Summary: 2 findings · 2 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 2 error(s): the fleet has agents that cannot be routed to, collide head-on, or cannot be read at all. Fix the errors before trusting delegation to this fleet.

===== skill-sprawl — skill duplicates, collisions, bloat =====
skill-sprawl v0.1.0 — audit · folder skills
2 markdown files seen · 2 skill candidates · 2 skills parsed · 0 unrecognized · 0 ignored (supporting docs) · walk: recursive (subfolders included)
Read-only: it edits nothing and runs nothing. It reads the skill definition files in the tree you point it at — files named SKILL.md, plus loose .md files that open with a frontmatter block; other .md files are counted as supporting docs and ignored.
Similarity: the Jaccard index over each description's set of lowercase alphanumeric word tokens. Collision at 0.50, near-identical at 0.90; the short-description floor is 40 characters; the oversized-body line is 500 lines; the discovery budget is 16000 listing characters (a reported figure). Token counts are estimates at chars/4. Thresholds are heuristics — see SKILL.md.

INVENTORY (2):
  notes-writer — 104 desc chars · body 2 lines · ~19 tokens est. · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md
  notes-writer — 104 desc chars · body 2 lines · ~19 tokens est. · notes-writer/SKILL.md
COLLECTION TOTALS: 2 skills · 4 body lines · ~38 tokens of body text (est., chars/4) · discovery listing 232 of 16000 budget chars

ERRORS — skills that cannot be discovered, collide head-on, are defined more than once, or cannot be read (2):
[DESCRIPTION_IDENTICAL] "notes-writer" + "notes-writer" · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md
  the descriptions of "notes-writer" and "notes-writer" are near-identical (token-set similarity 1.000, at or above the 0.90 line) — a router choosing between them has nothing to choose on, so discovery between them is a coin flip
  fix: differentiate the descriptions until each names work the other does not claim — or merge the two skills
[DUPLICATE_NAME] "notes-writer" · archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md
  the name "notes-writer" is defined by 2 files (archive/notes-writer/SKILL.md, notes-writer/SKILL.md) — which definition loads depends on scope order, so the collection does not reliably contain the skill you think it does
  fix: keep one definition per name across the whole tree, or rename until names are unique

Summary: 2 findings · 2 errors · 0 warnings · 0 info
Verdict: FAIL — 2 error(s): the collection has skills that cannot be discovered, collide head-on, are defined more than once, or cannot be read at all. Fix the errors before trusting discovery in this collection.

VERDICT: FINDINGS in clone-guard, secret-guard, hook-doctor, fleet-audit, skill-sprawl — read each module's section above before this setup runs.
(exit code 1)

The other direction — a clean setup

The same scan over a minimal tidy setup (one agent, one skill, an empty settings file) — head and verdict lines verbatim, module sections elided:

$ preflight-agent scan pf-control
preflight-agent v1.0.1 — scan · folder pf-control
5 module(s) run · 5 clean · 0 with findings · 0 skipped
...
VERDICT: CLEAN — every module that ran reported clean. CLEAN covers only what the five modules check; it is not a guarantee the setup is safe. Each module's limits are in its own section above.
(exit code 0)

合约

  • One JSON object per command with --json; argument and input errors are {"error": ...} with exit 2, including argparse errors in --json mode. No tracebacks. A module command's JSON is exactly the object that module printed standalone; scan's JSON nests those objects per module, plus a combined summary and clean verdict.
  • Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 error, identically for every module and for scan.
  • Read-only scanning. No scan writes to, executes, or installs anything in the target.
  • The one disclosed exception: secret-guard fix --apply writes — that is its job. It writes only the files you name, after a dry run by default, keeps a timestamped backup beside each changed file, and re-scans the rewrite before reporting it. It was ported intact from the standalone tool, and scan never invokes it.
  • 确定性的。 The same folder produces a byte-identical report on every run.
  • Each module's limits stand. Static checks prove what they cite and no more — every module prints its own honesty limits in its report, and SKILL.md collects them. A CLEAN verdict means "none of the checked problems were found", never "this setup is safe".

Why this suite exists — the merge

This pack is the merged flagship ordered by a fleet audit (FLEET-AUDIT-2026-11-04): 43 published tools were audited, and 18 of the quiet ones were ordered merged into 4 flagships so the fleet would be a few strong tools instead of dozens of shelf orphans. clone-guard, secret-guard, hook-doctor, fleet-audit and skill-sprawl — five standalone auditors, each already shipped and tested — became the modules of this suite.

The merge changed no engine: each module's code is byte-identical to its source tool's, its CLI shape and verdict vocabulary are unchanged, and it still reports its own source version (v0.1.0) inside its sections. The suite's own work is the dispatcher, the combined scan, and 24 new tests on top of the 276 the five source suites carried over — 300 in total.

Known note: the five engines are installed as top-level Python modules (clone_guard, secret_guard, hook_doctor, fleet_audit, skill_sprawl) alongside the preflight_agent dispatcher. If you also installed one of the original standalone tools, both installs provide the same module file with identical content — either copy behaves the same.

对于代理商

SKILL.md states the full command surface, the verdict vocabularies, the JSON contract and the limits — and makes preflight-agent itself installable as a skill: point your agent at this repo's SKILL.md and it will preflight setups before trusting them.

Install the skill bundle: this repo also ships the same SKILL.md as an installable bundle under skill/. To use it, copy the skill/ folder's SKILL.md into your agent's skills directory (for Claude Code: ~/.claude/skills/preflight-agent/SKILL.md), install the tool with pipx install preflight-agent, and your agent can then run a preflight scan before trusting any setup folder it is handed.

Tests

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

300 tests: the five source suites ported unchanged (56 + 57 + 44 + 58 + 61 = 276 — the only edit is each suite's EXAMPLES path, since examples now live per-module under examples/<module>/) plus 24 dispatcher/scan tests covering target discovery, skipped-with-reason reporting, the combined JSON shape, exit-code aggregation, and the proof that scan never invokes fix. Fixtures are fictional; the secrets in them are fake.

诚实的限度

  • Static evidence only. clone-guard reports surfaces that would execute, not what the code does once running; a CLEAN scan is never a safety guarantee.
  • secret-guard's scope is JSON configs it can parse. Values under ordinary key names outside env blocks, and TOML/YAML configs, are out of scope — and a secret that was ever committed stays leaked after moving it: rotate it.
  • hook-doctor judges hooks against a static rule table. It never runs a hook, so runtime behaviour (a script that exists but misbehaves) is invisible to it.
  • fleet-audit / skill-sprawl similarity is a heuristic — a token-set Jaccard index at stated thresholds (collision 0.50, near-identical 0.90, short-description floor 40 chars, discovery budget 16,000 listing chars): a reported figure, not a platform guarantee.
  • scan's discovery is a convention, stated above: it audits the settings/config/agents/skills locations it looks for. A setup that keeps those elsewhere needs the module commands pointed at the real paths.
  • Python-only implementation, terminal-text reports. No daemon, no watcher, no auto-remediation beyond secret-guard fix, no score — a receipt, not a rating.

请参阅 CONTRIBUTING.md。 The evidence discipline is the product: a finding is issued only on what the files show, and contributions are held to that. Open an issue with the folder (or a minimal fixture); that is exactly the feedback that improves the checks.

preflight-agent is itself an audit tool, so its own posture is simple: it has no network code, no dependencies, and its scans never execute what they read. See SECURITY.md for how to report a problem.
